land.text: Portuguese Angola, including the exclave province of Cabinda: 'The Angolan province of Cabinda is an exclave on the Atlantic coast.'

predecessors.note: Independence 11 November 1975; Cliopatria's Estado Novo row still draws Angola inside its 1967-1975 shape.

capitals.name: Luanda
capitals.note: 'The capital and most populous city is Luanda.' The FNLA-UNITA rival government of November 1975 sat at Huambo (see the unita dossier).

correction.text: new keyframe, years only: the shape of Cliopatria's 1976 row (Angola with Cabinda) holds from independence on 11 November 1975

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria's first Angola shape begins in 1976 but the infobox says 'Granted: 11 November 1975' and the Alvor Agreement 'set the country's independence date for 11 November 1975'. Cliopatria's Estado Novo 1967-1975 shape still holds Angola in 1975; the compiler should hand the land to this dossier at the found event.

1,257,376 km2 for 1976-2023 against the infobox 1,246,700 km2 (ratio 1.01). The shape reaches 4.41 S, so it holds Cabinda. The gazetteer shows 21 cells over neighbouring countries and 56 Angolan cells missing out of about 4,900, a border-precision difference, not an error of extent.

correction.text: the 2024 shape plus Cabinda: 'The Angolan province of Cabinda is an exclave on the Atlantic coast.'

keyframe_review.note: The 2024 shape stops at 5.89 S (1,250,482 km2): Cabinda (about 7,000 km2, 4.5-5.7 S) is missing. Cliopatria's Estado Novo row ends in 2024 with a 6,894 km2 patch at Cabinda (its 1979-2023 shape is the same patch, overlapping this row's 1976-2023 shape, which already holds Cabinda). With Cabinda back the area is 1.257 M km2, the 1976 figure.

region.text: Angola within the Alvor-era colonial borders, Cabinda included

ledger.note: 1975: Angola becomes independent from Portugal. Infobox 'Granted: 11 November 1975'; the Alvor Agreement 'set the country's independence date for 11 November 1975'; 'Angola achieved independence in 1975 as a one-party Republic.' The civil war began the same month.

region.text: the provinces of the towns the SADF columns captured in 1975: Xangongo (Cunene), Sá da Bandeira/Lubango (Huíla), Moçâmedes (Namibe), Benguela and Lobito (Benguela), Luso (Luena); 'penetrated more than 500 km into Angola'

ledger.note: 1975: South African columns hold the south and the Benguela coast. Operation Savannah page: on 9 August a SADF patrol occupied the Ruacana-Calueque complex; 'Zulu captured Roçadas (Xangongo) by 20, Sá da Bandeira (Lubango) by 24 and Moçâmedes by 28 October'; 'On 6 and 7 November 1975 Zulu captured the harbour cities of Benguela (terminal of the Benguela railroad) and Lobito. The towns and cities captured by the SADF were given to UNITA.'; Task Force X-Ray overran Luso on 10 December 1975. The advance on the coast was stopped short of Novo Redondo ('the SADF was unable to break through FAPLA defences'), so Cuanza Sul is not included. The Border War page: 'By early November, the three SADF columns had captured eighteen major towns and cities' and 'penetrated more than 500 km into Angola'. The month is the independence month (the Angolan state exists from 11 November); the SADF crossed on 9 August and took most of the towns in October. The provinces are the researcher's reading of the towns named: the columns held a corridor, not whole provinces.

region.text: Huambo and the Bie Plateau, the highland interior UNITA controlled much of

ledger.note: 1975: the civil war opens over the highlands. UNITA 'was nearly destroyed in November 1975, but it managed to survive and set up a second government, the Democratic People's Republic of Angola, in the provincial capital of Huambo' and 'controlled much of the highland's interior, notably the Bie Plateau' (1975-2002). The Angolan Civil War page: the war 'began immediately after Angola became independent from Portugal in November 1975'. The extent held varied by year; the region is the researcher's reading of 'much of the highland's interior'.

region.text: Huambo, 'the capital of the Democratic People's Republic of Angola' declared by Savimbi on independence

ledger.note: 1975: Huambo passes to the FNLA-UNITA government. Huambo page: upon independence in 1975 Savimbi declared Huambo the capital of the Democratic People's Republic of Angola; the UNITA page has UNITA setting up that government 'in the provincial capital of Huambo' and the Angolan Civil War page dates the proclamation to 23 November 1975 (see the wars note). Mirror of the found event of the unita dossier; the month is the independence month, the page gives no day for when the MPLA lost control of the city.

region.text: 'the MPLA took the city back on 8 February 1976 with the help of Cuban troops'

ledger.note: 1976: the MPLA takes Huambo back. Huambo page: 'the MPLA took the city back on 8 February 1976 with the help of Cuban troops'. The Cuban force had risen to 11,000 by February 1976 (Angolan Civil War page, see the wars note).

region.text: the provinces of the towns the SADF columns captured in 1975: Xangongo (Cunene), Sá da Bandeira/Lubango (Huíla), Moçâmedes (Namibe), Benguela and Lobito (Benguela), Luso (Luena); 'penetrated more than 500 km into Angola'

ledger.note: 1976: South Africa withdraws from Angola. 'The withdrawal commenced in February 1976 and formally ended a month later.' The Angolan Civil War page: 'the South African military withdrew in February 1976.' The Operation Savannah page says Luso served 'as a supply point until the South Africans finally departed Angola in early January 1976' and the Border War page that the SADF 'made the decision around Christmas of 1975 to begin withdrawing': the pages differ by two months; the Border War page's March is kept as the formal end.

region.text: Cunene province: 'up to 5,000 SADF soldiers occupied Cunene province, Angola'; Xangongo taken 24-25 August, Ongiva on 27-28 August 1981

ledger.note: 1981: Operation Protea, South Africa occupies Cunene. The Operation Protea page: 'up to 5,000 SADF soldiers occupied Cunene province, Angola'; the operation ran from 23 August 1981, Xangongo fell on 25 August, 'By 12h08, Ongiva was under South African control' on 28 August; 'By 2 September all units were back in SWA/Namibia.' The page does not say the SADF stayed; the span to 1988 is a bridge: the Operation Askari page has 'Small SADF units remained in Calueque, N'Giva and Xangongo' in January 1984 and the Angolan Civil War page gives South African intervention 'from 1981 to 1987'. The Lusaka Accords page: the 1984 accord 'was annulled de facto on 16 May 1985, and an escalation of hostilities followed'.

region.text: southern Angola held by the SADF (Cunene, with the 1987-88 fighting at Cuito Cuanavale in Cuando Cubango not drawn)

ledger.note: 1988: South Africa leaves Angola. The Tripartite Accord (Angola) page: 'The South African Army left Angola by 30 August 1988, before the conditions for Cuba's withdrawal had been agreed', and the accord 'provided for the retreat of South African forces from Angola, which had already taken place by 30 August'; the accords were signed in New York on 22 December 1988. The date is the page's; the province (Cunene) is the researcher's reading, carried from the 1981 event, since the page names no province.

region.text: Huambo, taken by UNITA on 7 March 1993 after a 55-day battle

ledger.note: 1993: UNITA takes Huambo. 'UNITA began a 55-day battle over Huambo' after the 1992 election and gained control of it on 7 March 1993; 'By August 1993, UNITA had gained control over 70% of Angola.' Only Huambo is named: the 70% cannot be mapped from the pages.

region.text: 'A large offensive gave back to the Government the control of Huambo on 9 November'

ledger.note: 1994: the government retakes Huambo. Huambo page: 'The armed conflict flared up again in August 1994. A large offensive gave back to the Government the control of Huambo on 9 November', and soon after all other provincial capitals; the UNITA headquarters then moved to Jamba and, 'soon after signing the protocol', to Bailundo (50 km north). The Angolan Civil War page: 'the government's military successes in 1994 forced UNITA to sue for peace' and 'By November 1994, the government had taken control of 60% of the country' (from UNITA's 70% of August 1993); the Lusaka Protocol was signed on 31 October 1994 and the ceasefire on 20 November. The region is the province as in the 1993 loss: Bailundo, which the Huambo page says the government retook only in October 1999, lay inside it, so the province overstates the government's hold in 1995-99.

2002: the civil war ends. Infobox '11 November 1975 - 4 April 2002'. The Angola page: 'On 22 February 2002, government troops killed Jonas Savimbi' and in April 2002 'UNITA agreed to give up its armed wing'.

region.text: the Bie Plateau without Huambo, which returned in November 1994: UNITA's highland interior

ledger.note: 2002: the rest of the highlands returns to the government. UNITA 'agreed to a ceasefire with the government' in April 2002, six weeks after Savimbi's death, and 'In August 2002 UNITA officially gave up its armed wing'. Huambo itself was back with the government since 9 November 1994 (Huambo page) and the town of Bailundo since October 1999 ('The Government retook the town of Bailundo in October 1999'); the Angolan Civil War page is silent on 1999, so the year here is the ceasefire's.

wars.name: Angolan Civil War

zones.text: Huambo and the Bie Plateau, UNITA's highland interior

wars.outcome: MPLA government victory: Savimbi killed on 22 February 2002 and a ceasefire on 4 April 2002; UNITA gave up its armed wing in August 2002.
wars.note: Three periods of major fighting: 1975-1991, 1992-1994 and 1998-2002. FNLA and UNITA proclaimed the Democratic People's Republic of Angola at Huambo on 23 November 1975; Zaire sent troops for the FNLA in 1975; Cuban troops rose from 5,500 (December 1975) to 11,000 (February 1976) and the last left in 1991; FLEC declared a 'Republic of Cabinda' in 1975 and Cuban forces mopped it up in 1975-76 (no ground held on the page).

wars.name: South African Border War

zones.text: the land the SADF held in Angola: the provinces of the towns captured in 1975-76 (Operation Savannah) and Cunene in 1981-88

wars.outcome: Military stalemate and the Tripartite Accord: South African forces left Namibia, Cuban forces left Angola, and South West Africa became the Republic of Namibia on 21 March 1990.
wars.note: Infobox '26 August 1966 - 21 March 1990'. The Angolan theatre: Calueque occupied 9 August 1975, Operation Savannah to the withdrawal of February-March 1976; the later 1981-88 incursions are not dated on this page.

certainty.note: The external frontiers are the colonial treaty lines ('did not achieve its present borders until the early 20th century'; the Berlin Conference set the colony's borders, per the Angola page). The line between government and UNITA held land (1975-2002) is soft and is not fixed by the pages opened.

notes: Cliopatria rows: People's Republic of Angola 1976-2023 and 2024. (1) The 2024 shape lacks Cabinda; the Estado Novo row's 1979-2024 shape is a 6,894 km2 patch at Cabinda that overlaps this row's 1976-2023 shape (which already holds Cabinda): eu-21 (Estado Novo) should drop the patch; this dossier adds Cabinda back to the 2024 shape. (2) Independence is 11 November 1975 and Cliopatria starts in 1976: the 1975 keyframe is new, and Cliopatria's Estado Novo 1967-1975 shape also holds Angola in 1975. (3) The Angola page does not give the later renaming to 'Republic of Angola'; no rename event is recorded. (4) South African occupation: 1975-76 is placed by the Operation Savannah page (the provinces of the towns captured, a wide reading; Cuando Cubango, which Task Force Zulu crossed on 14 October, and Cuanza Sul are left out); 1981 is dated and placed by the Operation Protea page (Cunene, August 1981, units back in Namibia by 2 September); 1988-08 by the Tripartite Accord (Angola) page ('left Angola by 30 August 1988'). The span 1981-88 is a bridge with Cunene as the province: no page opened states a continuous occupation (Askari has small units at Calueque, N'Giva and Xangongo in January 1984; the Lusaka Accords page has the 1984 accord annulled on 16 May 1985; the Civil War page has intervention 'from 1981 to 1987' and Cuito Cuanavale in 1987-88). (5) UNITA's 'control over 70% of Angola' (August 1993) cannot be mapped from the pages opened; a gap-filler should find a map of UNITA-held areas for 1993-94 and 1999-2002. (6) The rebel state UNITA has its own dossier (unita). The FNLA-UNITA 'Democratic People's Republic of Angola' (Huambo, 23 November 1975) and FLEC's 1975 'Republic of Cabinda' have no dossier. (7) The 'Bie plateau' region of the gazetteer is the union of Benguela, Huambo, Bie and Cuanza Sul (about 180,000 km2): a wide reading of 'the highland's interior'. Page budget: 2 pages for the state (Angola, South African Border War) plus the Angolan Civil War and UNITA pages shared with the rebel dossier. (8) Huambo 1993-94: lost to UNITA on 7 March 1993 and regained by the government on 9 November 1994 (Huambo page; the page leaves the year to be inferred from 'flared up again in August 1994'); the earlier note that the retaking of Huambo was not dated, and the guess 1999-2000, are withdrawn. Bailundo (Huambo province, 50 km north of the city) was UNITA's headquarters from late 1994 and was retaken in October 1999 (Huambo page); no separate 1999 event is recorded because the ledger has no earlier UNITA gain of Bailundo to reverse and the 1994 gain is the whole province. Repair run of 2026-10-24 (reviewer finding of the same date).
